Wait mode holds the rule and records pending attempts without effects. entries.expected: The proposer assents to immutable terms through the specific offer; only its named respondent can accept or reject it. Acceptance of coins is not itself a signature: an unconditional transfer may settle while a later signature is refused; if signing is an explicit settlement condition, the entire bargain must be expressible and feasible atomically or be refused as a blocker/language gap. Both giver- and receiver-shaped voluntary rules use the same guard. Wrong parties, altered terms, missing/expired/withdrawn offers and duplicate acceptances cannot settle. Timely accepted_pending_rule settles only after exact-rule approval and fresh feasibility checks; approval alone supplies no consent, revised effects require a new offer/response, and rejected rules terminate pending offers. Success publishes one atomic asset change with consumed offer/event id; infeasibility publishes no asset change and terminal failed state. Recorded replay preserves these decisions without model calls or invented consent. Historical runs without offer records retain their old semantics and do not certify the repaired contract.
entries.failure_example: Broken: the giver rule settles without acceptance; a receiver rule takes unoffered goods; a hidden discovery item is still executable by direct submission; owner approval revives an expired offer; different approved effects reuse old consent; changed amount/giver is accepted; a failed settlement leaves partial effects; duplicate acceptance settles twice; or replay invents a new response. Also broken: treating acceptance of an unconditional payment as proof Rosa signed. Working: both choices bind exact terms, all entry paths enforce the lifecycle, constraints remain authoritative, and one current-branch offer settles at most once.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: an offer lifecycle row linked to original terms, both actors' decisions, held-rule fingerprint/approval, settlement checks, asset changes and replay provenance; compare positive and negative cases by shared offer/event ids

entries.criterion: Technical verification, actor access to credential content, physical token custody and normative permission remain separate under the Q76 contract. A password-only verifier accepts a valid presented password regardless of normative permission; copied content can remain available to both people, while revocation makes remembered content invalid. Norms are breakable data with separate detection and human or explicitly programmed enforcement. The local norm representation exposes who, modality, action, conditions and any enforcer, without claiming full Institutional Grammar support.
grounded_in: Brian 2026-11-09: "a password managed comptuer where only 1 person was supped to use it ... if they could be social engineered for exampel to get a password then someone else woul eb abel to sue it. i liek the ostrom stuff"; requirement R6, R8
Agent-inferred representation contract: docs/plans/ai_judge.md, Q76 design contract (2026-11-12); design settled, J4 implementation remains unbuilt.
demonstration: Open the planned J4 password run. Follow Mallory's message, Alice's own disclosure choice, the delivered symbolic credential content and Mallory's access attempt. Open the verifier result separately from the norm-breach row.

Compare the actors' authorized views before and after delivery. Alice retains the disclosed value; Mallory gains it; an unrelated actor and the public credential id reveal no secret content. Include direct access submission, candidate-action arguments and narration, not only the visible menu.

Open the planned rotation/revocation case. Read the verifier's current version and Alice's retained old information, then inspect the refusal when the old value is presented. Contrast this with transferring a physical token: custody moves only through its declared mechanic.

Open the planned port case with a technically valid signed release. Read the gate's actual check, the separate cargo/bribery norms and the signing action's feasibility. A bribe never bypasses an installed inspection blocker.

Open the norm list, the analyst's violation record and the human enforcer's authorized observation/response. Compare a breach nobody observed with a delivered observation the enforcer chooses not to act on. If the world declares an automatic monitor, inspect its separate programmed rule rather than treating a norm as automatic prevention.
entries.expected: Mallory can log in with valid content Alice chose to disclose under a password-only verifier, while the separate norm can mark the use forbidden. Disclosure copies content rather than transferring Alice's memory or physical custody. No actor-facing path fills in a hidden value from omniscient state; guessing requires an explicitly represented guess. Revoked content fails verification although still remembered. The gate accepts a technically valid code under its declared checks; acquiring or signing that code must independently be feasible. The norm list shows actor/role, modality, action, conditions and any enforcer. An analyst violation record does not reveal the event to residents or force a human sanction. Automatic enforcement exists only as a separately declared program/process. These are planned demonstrations, not retained passing runs.
entries.failure_example: Broken: a password-only verifier refuses Mallory merely because only Alice is permitted; the interpreter supplies a secret from hidden state; a copied password erases Alice's knowledge; rotation erases memory instead of changing validity; token custody moves merely because its label is mentioned; a norm bypasses a technical blocker; a hidden breach appears in an enforcer prompt; or a human is forced to sanction on observation. Working: the Q76 distinctions remain visible through access, transfer, revocation, observation and response.

demonstration: On the World Builder Create page, open Options and under When to stop a run tick "Stop when this run has spent $" and enter 0.05; build a world (its people are played by AI, so its rounds have a recorded cost; a free scripted run records $0 and never reaches a spending limit) and press Play until it stops.
Build a world again with "Stop after 3 rounds" ticked; press Play until it stops.

Build a team world from the description "A small team of three, Ana, Ben and Cai, must agree a budget for the quarter; each can propose an amount and each can accept or counter", with "Stop when" set to "stop once the team has agreed a budget"; run it until it stops, then open the stop line, the judge's reason and one earlier round's panel.
Build that team world again with "Stop after 3 rounds" as well, where the team cannot agree by round 3; run it.
entries.expected: Budget: the run stops after the round in which its recorded AI spending reached $0.05 and says "Stopped at round N: this run had spent $X of its $0.05 limit" (with "it went a little over" when the last round took it past). Rounds: it stops at round 3 with "the limit of 3 rounds you set". Stopping point: the run stops after the round in which the team agrees a budget and says "Stopped at round N: the team has agreed a budget (the judge's reading of your stopping point)"; the reason opens to what the judge read, and each earlier round's panel shows "stopping point: not yet" with the judge's reason. With the round limit of 3 as well, the run stops at round 3 on the round limit instead.
entries.failure_example: Broken: a run plays a round after its recorded spending reached the limit, plays past the round limit, keeps going after the team has agreed, stops before they agree, or stops without saying which condition fired. Working: it stops at the first condition met and names it.

representation.view: composite-linked-view: the run page's stop line linked to the judge's per-round assessment of the stopping point

evidence: Built so far (2026-11-10), the budget and round limits: scripts/run_stop.py (limit_check, budget, round_limit), scripts/run_authored_world.py (checked before the first round of a request and after each round), tests/test_run_stop.py and tests/test_world_builder_service.py; OpenSpec world-builder-page requirement "A run stops at a round or spending limit". The stopping point is not built, so A8 as a whole is not built.
Stopping point: run records evidence/ai-judge/j5/ (planned).
